retell: China's leaders told officials not to rush blindly into high tech, so the AI boom does not turn into a bubble that costs a lot of money.
what: told officials to avoid blind rushes into high tech
why: so the AI boom does not become a costly bubble that loses people money

retell: A new company called TypeSafe AI got almost a billion dollars for some 'model' that gives odds instead of words, which might mean machines make business decisions.
what: raised nearly a billion dollars for a model that gives odds instead of words
why: business decisions may be handed to machines
problem: 'a model' is industry jargon (a stranger hears a fashion or toy model), so 'a model that gives odds instead of words' does not say it is an A I that predicts chances rather than writing text.
fix: On the markets. Start-up TypeSafe A I raised nearly a billion dollars for an A I that predicts odds, not words, so business choices may pass to machines.

retell: Two companies, OpenAI and Anthropic, are reportedly getting ready for a big AI attack on banks or power that insiders think will come within a year.
what: are reportedly bracing for a big AI attack on banks or power
why: banks and the power supply could be hit within a year
problem: 'an-thropic' is never introduced (a stranger does not know that it or OpenAI are A I companies), so 'insiders' has nothing to be inside of; the name needs a short description.
fix: Next, safety. A I firms OpenAI and an-thropic reportedly brace for a big A I attack on banks or power, which insiders expect within a year.

retell: A start-up called Feather Robotics made a human-like robot with two arms on wheels that carries light things and costs under thirty thousand dollars, so small teams can buy one.
what: launched a wheeled two-armed humanoid robot for light loads, priced under thirty thousand dollars
why: small teams can afford a robot helper

retell: Anthropic, a chatbot company, will ban people from being needlessly cruel to its Claude AI starting in November, but it has not said what counts as cruel.
what: will bar users from being needlessly cruel to its Claude AI from November
why: Claude users could be barred without knowing exactly what counts as cruel

retell: A contractor working for the server company Super Micro admitted sneaking Nvidia AI chips to buyers in China, which breaks US rules.
who: a contractor for server maker Super Micro
what: admitted smuggling Nvidia AI chips to Chinese buyers
why: it broke US rules meant to keep the best chips away from China

retell: Nikon took back a microscope video prize from a Chinese scientist who used AI, because experts noticed the cells looked fake.
what: stripped its microscope video prize from a Chinese scientist who used AI
why: experts caught that the cells looked fake, so AI fakes are reaching science prizes
problem: 'the cells' are never introduced: the line never says the prize video showed cells, so a stranger asks 'which cells?'.
fix: In science. Camera maker Nikon stripped its microscope video prize from a Chinese scientist who used A I, after experts saw the cells he showed looked fake.

retell: A product manager in Spain who never studied astronomy used AI to find what might be a new planet, and NASA will check it next month.
who: a product manager in Spain with no astronomy training
what: used AI to spot a possible planet
why: it shows ordinary people can make discoveries with AI; NASA checks it next month

retell: Amazon wants its shop kept out of some Meta AI 'agent' thing, and a study says batteries are now cheaper than gas turbines at data centres.
what: Amazon wants its store out of Meta's AI agent; batteries are now cheaper than gas turbines for data centres
problem: 'Meta's A I agent' is jargon and 'wants its store out of' it is unclear (out of what?); 'data centre gas turbines' stacks three nouns; neither item says why it matters to people, and a why cannot be added without new facts.
fix: Also in the full report. Amazon wants Meta's A I helper kept off its store. And a study says batteries now cost less than gas turbines for data centres.

retell: China and a UN group both say AI might be a bubble, so next week check the big banks' reports to see how much people borrow to buy stocks.
what: both warn of an AI bubble; next week's big bank results show how much is borrowed to buy shares
why: a bubble can burst and cost people money, and heavy borrowing to buy shares shows how risky it is
